Subject: RE: Pricing and credits for replacement evaluation (internal)

Chloe / Aditya —

I ran the usage file through our price model. Key assumptions: their current vendor effective unit cost = $0.00095/token (avg); Pivotal forecasts ~420M tokens/month for Q4 onboarding. Two quick levers that will look good in the scorecard:

1) One-time onboarding credit: $120k applied up-front to first invoice (covers estimated migration engineering + credits).
2) Tiered rebate: 6% rebate on committed monthly spend for first 6 months if they commit to 12 months term; rebate steps to 10% if they commit to 24 months and show QoQ growth >= 10%.

Net blended unit after credit (first 3 months) comes to ~ $0.00071/token assuming they ramp to 80% usage quickly (spreadsheet attached).

Constraints/notes:
- Credit requires a signed SOW and agreed migration milestones (we should include a 90-day clawback if they cancel).
- Rebate applied as a dollar credit monthly; needs a minimum monthly commit of $75k to qualify.
- We should avoid upfront deep discounts to the base rate; prefer rebate against committed usage so list price stays intact.

I'll attach a price_comparison_spreadsheet.xlsx with scenarios.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed transition economics and next steps

Eleanor / Procurement —

Thanks for the time this week. Per our internal analysis, here's a concise offer you can use in the supplier scorecard:

Proposal summary (high level):
- One-time onboarding credit: $120,000 applied to first invoice. This covers migration assistance and an initial run of our evaluation cluster.
- Tiered rebate schedule (applies to committed monthly spend):
  * 12-month term: 6% monthly rebate for first 6 months (monthly credit applied to invoice)
  * 24-month term: 10% monthly rebate for first 6 months + eligibility for a PvP technical migration workshop (onsite/virtual)
- Minimum monthly commit to qualify: $75,000
- Blended first-quarter effective unit (illustrative): ~$0.00072/token (see attached spreadsheet for sensitivity by ramp)

Operational guardrails:
- Credits issued as invoice credits; onboarding credit paid after initial kick-off and completion of milestone 1 (data ingress checklist).
- 90-day clawback on onboarding credit if contract terminates without notice; rebate applies only to paid, eligible invoices.

Attachments: redwood_transition_credit_terms.pdf (draft terms), price_comparison_spreadsheet.xlsx (scenario math)

If that looks workable I can:
- Share a short SOW with milestone language and the credit clause for your legal/procurement to review (I included a marked SOW for internal review).
- Draft HubSpot deal update (link below) and prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment once procurement confirms term length.

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/PD-2026-118

Primary ask: can procurement confirm whether a tiered rebate or a single lump-sum credit is preferred? If they prefer lump-sum, we can do a one-time $145k credit in lieu of tiered structure for 12-months.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to walk procurement through the mechanics.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
